column1: # Latin, the spoken language of the early Empire, in Classical phonemes
# (vowel length kept; c = k, qu = kʷ, v = w, ae = ai).
# Nouns and adjectives are given in their accusative stem without -m
# (lupu, kane, nokte): the form the Romance languages continue. Verbs are
# present stems with their theme vowel (3rd singular without -t).
# Final -m, already weak in speech, is left off: nominative and accusative
# share the stem. Endings are simplified to one exponent per category; Latin fused number
# and case, which the engine models as separate affixes.
# Hand-written from standard dictionaries (Lewis & Short; de Vaan 2008).
# Concepts left out are coined in Latin's own sounds and marked as coined.

column2: Spoken Latin of the early Empire: five long and five short vowels, case endings, prepositions, no articles yet.
Lewis & Short; de Vaan, Etymological Dictionary of Latin (2008); forms simplified by hand
